summary.problem: The arrowhead picker popup could overflow off the edge of the screen because the visual popup surface was an inner div that Radix's collision-avoidance system could not measure or reposition.
summary.solution: Move the picker class and all visual props directly onto the Radix Popover.Content element and remove the inner wrapper div, so Radix measures and repositions the exact element the user sees.

plain.title: Arrowhead picker stays inside the screen
plain.problem: The arrowhead picker could slide off the edge of the screen because the built-in collision-avoidance system didn't know where the visible edge of the popup was.
plain.fix: The popup surface is now the single element that Radix measures, so it correctly nudges the picker back into view whenever it would overflow.

steps.title: Arrowhead picker overflows the viewport edge
steps.headline: The picker slides off the screen edge
steps.say: When you open the arrowhead picker near the edge of the screen, the popup disappears past the viewport boundary instead of shifting to stay visible.
steps.narration: When a user opens the arrowhead style picker near the edge of the editor, the popup overflows out of view instead of nudging itself to stay on screen. Radix has built-in collision avoidance for exactly this scenario, so something must be stopping it from working correctly.

items: Arrowhead picker popup is clipped or invisible near viewport edges
Popup appears to slide outside the editor boundary

steps.title: Radix measures the wrong element for collision
steps.headline: Radix measured the wrong element for collision
steps.say: The visible popup box was a plain inner div, not the element Radix tracks. Radix only corrects the position of its own element, so the inner box still overflowed.
steps.narration: Radix Popover places its content element in the DOM and watches its bounding box to decide whether to flip or shift the popup to avoid the viewport edge. Before this change, the Radix element had no visual appearance of its own — all the background, border, and padding belonged to a plain inner div. Because Radix only repositions its own element, it was nudging an invisible box while the real visible box kept overflowing. The measurement confirms this: at BASE the picker element's computed position is absolute and it carries no Radix data-side attribute, meaning Radix's tracking never reached the visible surface.

beats.heading: How it was structured
beats.text: The `Popover.Content` had no class and no visual style. The visual popup surface was an inner `div.picker`. The BASE measurement confirms `position:"absolute"` on the picker and `pickerHasDataSide:false` — Radix's own `data-side` attribute was not present on the element the user could see.

lines.annotation: Radix tracks this element for collision avoidance — but it carries no visual style. `pickerHasDataSide:false` at BASE confirms Radix's tracking attribute never reached the visible surface.
The visible popup surface: all visual appearance lives on this child div, not on the element Radix repositions.

steps.title: Removing position:absolute alone is not enough
steps.headline: The CSS fix alone is not enough
steps.say: Simply removing the absolute positioning leaves the visual styling on a wrapper that Radix still does not measure. The right fix is to collapse the two layers into one — so the next step does exactly that.
steps.narration: You might think just removing position absolute from the inner div would fix the overflow. The ablation confirms it does not: applying only the CSS removal to the base still reports the bug present. The core problem is the two-layer structure itself — Radix measures the outer element it owns, while the visual popup lives on the inner div. The right fix is to make those two elements one.

beats.heading: The constraint
beats.text: The inner div carries the `picker` class with all its visual styles. The ablation confirms that removing `position: absolute` from this class alone (without restructuring the DOM) leaves the overflow bug present.

lines.annotation: Ablation: removing only this line leaves the bug present — the DOM mismatch between Radix's tracked element and the visible surface is the actual cause.

sources.ref: Ablation: ONLY [IconPicker.scss#1] → bug (CSS removal alone does not fix)

steps.title: Move all visual props onto Popover.Content, drop the inner wrapper
steps.headline: Popup surface collapsed to one element
steps.say: The picker class and all visual styling move directly onto the Radix element, and the inner wrapper div is deleted. Ablation confirms this single change is sufficient to fix the overflow.
steps.narration: The fix collapses two elements into one: the class name, dialog role, and alignment offset all move onto the Radix element directly, and the inner wrapper is gone. Now when Radix decides the popup needs to shift, it moves the visible surface itself. The ablation confirms this change alone is sufficient — applying only it to the base code fixes the bug. At the fixed version, the picker carries Radix's own tracking marker, proof that Radix now sees the right element.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: All visual and semantic attributes move onto `Popover.Content`; the inner `div.picker` wrapper is removed. An `alignOffset` of 12 is also added. The HEAD measurement confirms `position:"static"` and `pickerHasDataSide:true` — Radix now tracks the visible surface directly. Ablation: this hunk alone fixes the bug.

lines.annotation: Now both the Radix-tracked element and the visual popup surface. HEAD: `pickerHasDataSide:true`, `position:"static"`. Applying this hunk alone fixes the bug.
`picker` class moved here from the deleted inner div — background, shadow, and padding now live on the element Radix repositions.

steps.title: Remove now-orphaned position:absolute from stylesheet
steps.headline: Stray absolute positioning removed from styles
steps.say: With the inner div deleted, its absolute-positioning CSS rule is removed as cleanup. Ablation confirms this CSS change alone does not fix the bug.
steps.narration: With the inner wrapper gone, its position-absolute CSS rule would do nothing useful. Leaving it in place would be harmless, but cleaning it up keeps the stylesheet consistent. The ablation measurement confirms that applying this CSS change alone to the base code does not fix the overflow — the real fix is the DOM restructure in the previous step.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: `position: absolute` is removed from `.picker` in the stylesheet. Ablation confirms this change alone does not fix the overflow bug — it is cleanup that follows from the DOM restructure.

lines.annotation: Cleanup only — ablation shows removing this CSS alone leaves the overflow bug present.

steps.title: Mobile-specific side direction and offset removed
steps.headline: Mobile layout branch removed from picker
steps.say: The picker previously opened to the right on phones. Whether this was a deliberate UX choice or a workaround for the overflow is untested — the app did not build when this hunk was applied in isolation.
steps.narration: Before this PR, on mobile the picker was configured to open to the right of its trigger rather than below it, with a smaller gap. This could have been a workaround for the same overflow bug on small screens, or a deliberate mobile UX choice. The ablation could not produce a verdict for this hunk because the app failed to build when it was applied in isolation, so whether it is needed for the fix, or is independent cleanup, is not measured.

beats.heading: How it was before
beats.text: On mobile the popup opened to the `right` at a smaller `sideOffset`. This required reading the editor interface to detect the phone form factor.

lines.annotation: Only used to derive `isMobile`. Dropped along with the mobile branch.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: The mobile branch is gone. `side` is always `"bottom"`, `sideOffset` is always `12`, and the `useEditorInterface` import and call are removed.

lines.annotation: Always opens downward. Whether this is safe on mobile is untested by the ablation (build failure when hunk applied alone).

notes: Ablation verdict for this hunk is unavailable: applying it alone caused a build failure (removing useEditorInterface while the old two-div structure and its isMobile reference still exist breaks the build). Whether removing the mobile branch is required for the fix, or is independent cleanup, is therefore not measured.
That side="right" on mobile was a workaround for the same overflow bug — rather than a deliberate UX choice — is the analyzer's inference and is not stated by the author.

sources.ref: mobile branch as possible overflow workaround

skippedHunks.reason: removed unused import of useEditorInterface (cleanup after s6 removes the only call site)

openQuestions.question: Was `side="right"` on mobile actually a deliberate UX choice rather than a workaround — and if so, should the picker still open to the right on phones?
openQuestions.short: Was the mobile right-side layout intentional UX or a workaround?
openQuestions.why: The author removes it without comment and the ablation could not test this hunk in isolation due to a build failure.

openQuestions.question: Is `alignOffset={12}` the right value? It shifts the popup 12 px along the alignment axis, which could misalign it with its trigger on some trigger sizes.
openQuestions.short: Is alignOffset 12 the right amount for all trigger sizes?
openQuestions.why: `alignOffset` is a new prop not present in the base code. Its value was chosen without an explanation in the commit, and the trigger button size may vary.
